categoryMeta.description: Hill, trail, climbing, and rolling-terrain workouts.

workouts.title: Recreational Introductory Short Hill Sprints
workouts.summary: An easy introduction to short uphill speed play designed to stimulate neuromuscular power with minimal impact forces.
workouts.riskReason: Short explosive uphill strides introduce transient high tendon forces; walking recovery keeps risk manageable.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Jog segments very slowly. Sprints should feel fast, powerful, and vertical, around 90% maximal effort.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Let heart rate spike; ensure it fully drops during long walking recoveries.
intensityGuide.rpeGuide: Uphill sprints RPE 8/10. Jog base RPE 3/10.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization Warm-up
warmup.description: 5 mins slow walking with ankle circles and light high-knees.

mainSet.name: 6 × 8-Sec Hill Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 8 seconds up a moderate hill (6-8% grade) focusing on tall posture and explosive knee drive, followed by 90 seconds of slow walking back down recovery.

easier.description: Reduce main set to 4 repetitions with 2-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: 4 × 8-Sec Hill Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 8 seconds up a moderate hill, walk 120 seconds.

harder.description: Increase main set to 8 repetitions with 90-second recoveries.

mainSet.name: 8 × 8-Sec Hill Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 8 seconds up a moderate hill, walk 90 seconds.

coachingNotes: Focus on quick foot turnover and a tall, forward-leaning posture. Do not strain your shoulders.
Ensure you are fully warm before attempting the first sprint.
This is a neuromuscular session, not an endurance session. Ensure complete recovery.
commonMistakes: Jogging down too fast and accumulating muscle fatigue.
safetyNotes: Calf and Achilles strain risk. Never do these cold.
Stop immediately if sharp heel or calf pain occurs.

shareCard.purposeText: An easy introduction to uphill speed play to build neuromuscular power.

mainSet.name: 10 × 10-Sec Hill Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 10 seconds up a steep hill, walk 90 seconds.

coachingNotes: Focus on pure explosive power during the sprints. Do not jog.

workouts.title: Developing Trail Fartlek 30-Min
workouts.summary: A continuous 30-minute speed play session on rolling dirt paths incorporating easy pickups.
workouts.riskReason: Variable intensity segments on unstable trail surfaces introduce moderate ankle roll risks.

intensityGuide.primaryTarget: progressive short trail speed play effort
intensityGuide.paceGuide: Pickups at target threshold pace; recovery segments are easy jogging.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high Zone 2, rising to Zone 3 inside pickups.
intensityGuide.rpeGuide: Pickups RPE 6/10. Base jog RPE 3/10.

warmup.name: Gentle Joint Mobilization
warmup.description: 5 mins of slow walking and ankle mobilization.

mainSet.name: 30-Min Trail Fartlek

mainSet.description: Run 20 minutes continuously.

harder.description: Increase trail fartlek to 40 minutes continuous with 8 pickups.

mainSet.name: 40-Min Trail Fartlek
mainSet.description: Run 40 minutes continuously.

coachingNotes: Focus on smooth, relaxed running form. Do not sprint.
Prioritize a smooth, conversational rhythm for your base jog segments.
Enjoy the variation in effort. It shouldn't feel stressful.
commonMistakes: Running the pickups too fast, forcing walking recoveries.
safetyNotes: Warm up thoroughly before beginning.
Ensure your posture remains tall and vertical during faster phases.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Pickups at target 5K race effort; recoveries are active float jogs.

intensityGuide.rpeGuide: Pickups RPE 7-8/10. Recoveries RPE 4-5/10.

workouts.title: Advanced Downhill Control and Leg Yield
workouts.summary: An advanced neuromuscular training session focusing on eccentric quad strength and dynamic posture control during descent.
workouts.riskReason: Fast descents introduce massive eccentric joint impact forces; strict form is required to prevent patellar overload.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Outward leg warm-up at relaxed conversational pace; descent repetitions at controlled target race pace.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate will remain elevated in Zone 2 and Zone 3 throughout.
intensityGuide.rpeGuide: Descent repetitions RPE 7/10. Ascent walk RPE 3/10.

warmup.name: Gentle Joint Mobilization
warmup.description: 5 mins of slow walking and ankle mobilization.

mainSet.name: 5 × Downhill Control Reps
mainSet.description: Run 2 minutes downhill at a controlled, progressive pace on a gentle descent (4-6% grade) focusing on tall posture and light foot strikes, followed by walking back up to recover.

easier.description: Reduce descent repetitions to 3, keeping grade very gentle.

mainSet.name: 3 × Downhill Control Reps
mainSet.description: Run 3 reps of 2 minutes downhill, walk up 180 seconds.

harder.description: Increase descent repetitions to 8, with a slightly steeper descent.

mainSet.name: 8 × Downhill Control Reps
mainSet.description: Run 8 reps of 2 minutes downhill, walk up 180 seconds.

coachingNotes: Lean forward slightly from the ankles, matching the slope of the hill. Do not lean backward.
Keep your foot strikes light and quiet. Avoid heavy heel braking.
Use your arms for balance like a tightrope walker.
commonMistakes: Leaning backward and heavily heel-striking, overloading the knees.
Sprinting out of control down the hill.
safetyNotes: Patellar tendon and knee joint impact risk. Wear supportive trail shoes.
Stop immediately if sharp patellar or calf pain occurs.

shareCard.cardTitle: Advanced Downhill Control and Leg Yield
shareCard.purposeText: An advanced neuromuscular session to build eccentric quad strength.
